name: Upright piano (Yamaha)
note: An instrument recipe for the sampler (doc 24, Instruments, Sample preparation and Sampler rules). It describes exactly the files the prep step produced; nothing here is a tuning choice. type, id, name, version: what this is. source: where the recordings come from (library, folder url, license) and what the library's own note files say (notes). channels: channel count of every file. formats: each file exists once per format under root, as <file>.ogg (Ogg Opus, 48 kHz, 96 kbps stereo or 64 kbps mono, variable bitrate) and <file>.m4a (AAC-LC at the source rate, 128 kbps stereo or 96 kbps mono); the browser picks the first it can play. root: folder of the files, relative to the repo. layers: the number of velocity layers in the sustain set, layer 1 the quietest. sets: one entry per articulation: sus (sustain, pedal down or natural ring), nosus (dampers working), rel (release or key-off noise, played on note-off), pedal (sounds of the pedal mechanism). Each set has source (the library subfolder) and zones; a zone is one recorded key: note (scientific pitch, C4 = middle C, sharps written s in file names), midi (C4 = 60). measuredCents: the zone's measured pitch offset from 12-tone equal temperament at A4 = 440 Hz, in cents, as recorded; piano strings are inharmonic (partial n sits at n f0 sqrt(1 + B n^2)), so it is fitted from partials 1 to 6 (2 to 8 in the bass, where the fundamental is weak) over a window of the early sustain, each partial taken as the level-weighted centre of its unison-string cluster, and it is the pitch of the fitted first partial. Real pianos are stretch-tuned on purpose (bass flat, treble sharp); nothing has been corrected. tuneLayer: the layer the zone's number comes from (the middle one). tuneResidualCents: how far the found partials sit from the fit (root mean square, cents). tunePartials: which partials were found and used. layerSpreadCents: the largest difference between this zone's layers. inharmonicityB: the fitted B. unisonSplitCents: the widest spread seen inside one partial's cluster (a sign of unison strings tuned apart, which is heard as beating or chorus). tuneConfidence: 0 to 1, falls with fewer partials, a larger residual and a larger layer spread; below about 0.5 trust the ear over the number. layers: the files of the zone, quietest first; file is the path under root without extension; layer is its velocity layer and rr its round-robin take when the set has takes. peakDb: the file's sample peak in dBFS. attackRmsDb: the RMS level of its first 300 ms after the onset, in dBFS. Whether these levels mean anything depends on the source (see levels below). brightness: the share of energy above 1.5 times the note's fundamental (or 1 kHz, whichever is higher) in those first 300 ms, which should rise from layer to layer; in a very quiet file the noise floor can inflate it. lenS: length after the prep, in seconds. trimStartMs: how much was cut from the start (the onset, the first point above -50 dB of the file's peak, is kept with 3 ms before it). measuredCents on a layer is that file's own measurement. src: the original file name. Every file was cut where its 50 ms RMS fell to 60 dB below its peak, or at a maximum length (8 s at A0 falling evenly per semitone to 4 s at C8 for sustains, 2 s for releases), whichever came first, then given an equal-power fade over its last 250 ms (100 ms for releases and pedal sounds) so it ends in true silence. No gain was changed. levels: whether the source normalised each file (normalized true: the levels say nothing about how hard the key was played, so the sampler rebuilds the dynamic range from velocity with its own curve and must not re-gain the layers) or kept the recorded levels (normalized false: the layers already step up in level as they were played, and the sampler should play them at their own level). range: the lowest and highest sustain zone. problems: anything odd found while preparing, in plain words. The .m4a files decode about 23 ms longer than the .ogg files because AAC pads its last frame with silence; the start is in the same place in both. Yamaha upright: zones are a fourth or fifth apart (C and G), wider than the sampler's whole-tone rule; see problems.

source.notes: Folder 'Upright Piano, Yamaha', files Upright1_Sus_* and Upright1_Rel_*. Note.txt says this is a cleaned, recut and remastered version of the samples found in 'Upright No. 1' and under the same name in VSCO 2 CE. Zones are every fourth and fifth (C and G only), three velocity layers vl1 to vl3, and one to three round robins per layer, kept as -rr1, -rr2, -rr3. The source names are one octave low against scientific pitch (the file named C0 sounds C1, 32.7 Hz), confirmed by pitch measurement; the names here are corrected one octave up and src keeps the original.

levels.note: Recorded levels kept: v1 peaks near -25 to -44 dBFS, v3 near -0.2 to -7 dBFS. Play the layers at their own level.

problems: sus/G6-v1-rr1 (Upright1_Sus_G5_vl1_rr1.wav) looks like a bad take: its energy is almost all at 3128 Hz (G7, the second partial) with the G6 fundamental buried, it dies within 0.7 s (the other G6 takes ring 1.6 to 2.1 s) and its brightness is 0.85 against 0.003 to 0.016 for the others; its measured pitch (-36.6 cents) is not trustworthy. Suggest the sampler use sus/G6-v1-rr2 only.

sus/As0-v1-rr1 (Upright1_Sus_C0_vl1_rr1.wav) is the quietest file of the set (peak -38 dB, mostly rumble below the partials) and measures +47.7 cents where the other three A#0 takes measure +11 to +13; treat its number as unreliable.

The lowest Yamaha zone is odd: of the five files named C0, four (vl1 rr1, vl1 rr2, vl2 rr1, vl3 rr1) sound A#0 about 11 to 13 cents sharp and only vl3 rr2 sounds C1 (42 cents flat). They are placed as recorded: zone As0 with layers v1 (two takes), v2 and v3, and zone C1 with v3 only. That leaves C1 without soft layers and A#0 without a release sample (the release files named C0 were all left at C1).
sus: brightness does not rise with layer in 3 of 14 zones: G3 (v1 0.000, v2 0.045, v3 0.034); C4 (v1 0.020, v2 0.055, v3 0.051); G6 (v1 0.850, v2 0.003, v3 0.016)

sus: layers of the same key disagree in pitch by more than 5 cents in 4 zones (usually a high, fast-dying note or a unison that beats; the zone number uses the middle layer): As0 (v1 +47.7, v1 +11.2, v2 +12.7, v3 +11.1); G1 (v1 -16.5, v2 -23.9, v3 -18.6); C2 (v1 -2.8, v2 -15.4, v2 -15.9, v3 -15.0, v3 -15.4); G6 (v1 -36.6, v1 -0.4, v2 +1.7, v2 +1.7, v3 -0.8, v3 +0.4, v3 -0.9)

source files begin right at the attack with no silence before it (56 of 71 sus files, 45 of 71 rel files; first sample -39.4 to -5.7 dB below the file's peak). Nothing was cut from them; listen for a start click, and if one is heard a 1 to 2 ms fade-in at playback cures it.
sus/C6-v1-rr1 (Upright1_Sus_C5_vl1_rr1.wav): pitch check flagged it; reviewed by hand: fundamental at 1046 Hz (C6) with a weak second partial; the note is right
sus/As0-v1-rr1 (Upright1_Sus_C0_vl1_rr1.wav): placed at As0, not C1 as its name says, because it measurably sounds As0 (47.68 cents)
sus/As0-v1-rr2 (Upright1_Sus_C0_vl1_rr2.wav): placed at As0, not C1 as its name says, because it measurably sounds As0 (11.21 cents)
sus/As0-v2-rr1 (Upright1_Sus_C0_vl2_rr1.wav): placed at As0, not C1 as its name says, because it measurably sounds As0 (12.69 cents)
sus/As0-v3-rr1 (Upright1_Sus_C0_vl3_rr1.wav): placed at As0, not C1 as its name says, because it measurably sounds As0 (11.07 cents)

onset check: in 15 encoded files the -30 dB threshold crossing moved by more than 2 ms after encoding (codec ripple on a slow, quiet attack); cross-correlation of the first 80 ms against the processed WAV shows no shift in any of them (lag 0 to 0.02 ms), so the starts are in place

sus zones further apart than a whole tone (doc 24 sampler rule: at most 2 semitones): C1 to G1 (7 semitones), G1 to C2 (5 semitones), C2 to G2 (7 semitones), G2 to C3 (5 semitones), C3 to G3 (7 semitones), G3 to C4 (5 semitones), C4 to G4 (7 semitones), G4 to C5 (5 semitones), C5 to G5 (7 semitones), G5 to C6 (5 semitones), C6 to G6 (7 semitones), G6 to C7 (5 semitones)

rel: missing layers: C7 lacks v1
